questions.q: Breathing in: thorax volume and pressure...
questions.a: B) increase, decrease. Volume increases so pressure falls below atmospheric; air flows in.

questions.q: Products of anaerobic respiration in muscles?
Name the muscles between the ribs.
Gas that binds haemoglobin from smoke?
Big question: how are breathing, gas exchange and respiration linked and different?
questions.a: Breathing moves air; gas exchange moves O₂ into and CO₂ out of blood at the alveoli; respiration is the reaction in cells that uses O₂ and makes CO₂.

questions.q: Write the balanced symbol equation for aerobic respiration.
questions.model: Correct formulae for glucose, oxygen, carbon dioxide and water (1). Balance carbon (6CO₂), hydrogen (6H₂O), then oxygen (6O₂) (1).

questions.a: Large surface area; walls one cell thick (or good blood supply; moist).

questions.q: Explain how tar damages the airways.
questions.a: Tar damages cilia (1) so mucus is not cleared, causing infections and bronchitis (1). (Tar also contains carcinogens.)

questions.q: Describe how breathing in and out happens. Portal response box.
questions.a: In: intercostals contract, ribs up and out (1); diaphragm contracts and flattens (1); volume increases, pressure falls, air in (1). Out: intercostals relax, ribs down and in (1); diaphragm relaxes and domes (1); volume decreases, pressure rises, air out (1).
questions.model: Teacher writes breathing in as three linked points, then pupils write breathing out in the same structure.

questions.q: Describe an experiment to show that exhaled air contains more CO₂ than inhaled air.
questions.a: Two tubes of limewater (or hydrogencarbonate indicator) (1); breathe in through one, out through the other (1); exhaled tube turns milky (or yellow) faster (1); same volume and time (1).

questions.q: Explain why a sprinter keeps breathing deeply after a race.
questions.a: Anaerobic respiration made lactic acid (1); oxygen is needed to break it down (oxygen debt) (1); so breathing rate and depth stay high (1).
